1 cup chicken cooking broth: Toss the carrots and peas in butter for 3 minutes.
Add the rice and toast for 1 minute; add the hot broth.
Cook over a low heat for 15 minutes until the liquid is absorbed, add the chicken and leave to steam for 10 minutes.
Lightly crush the peas to reduce the risk of choking.
Cool quickly; 24 hours in the fridge.
Baked potato and vegetable croquettes
2 medium boiled potatoes
2 tablespoons grated carrot
Mash the potatoes; mix with the carrot, kashar and egg yolk.
Shape finger-thick croquettes from the mixture and coat in breadcrumbs.
Bake on a lined tray for 20 minutes, turning halfway, until golden.
Baking instead of frying is a lighter option.
Apple-cinnamon rice pudding
1 small apple, grated
Cook the rice in the water for 15 minutes until soft.
Add the milk and grated apple.
Cook over a low heat, stirring constantly, for 15–20 minutes until thick.
Divide into bowls and cool; sprinkle with cinnamon when serving.
The apple provides sweetness; there’s no need to add sugar.
Spinach with mince
60 g lean beef mince
2 cups chopped spinach
Fry the onion in olive oil for 2 minutes, then the mince for 5 minutes, breaking it up.
Add the spinach, rice and hot water; cook covered over a low heat for 20 minutes.
Serve with yogurt.
Wash the spinach well in several changes of water to remove the soil.
Chicken skewers (oven-baked)
100 g chicken breast, 2 cm cubes
A pinch of thyme and sweet paprika
Half a red pepper, roughly chopped
Mix the chicken with yogurt, olive oil and spices and leave in the fridge for at least 30 minutes.
Arrange the chicken and pepper on a tray (don’t use skewer sticks for children).
Bake for 18–20 minutes until the chicken is completely white inside.
Break into small pieces and serve with bulgur pilaf.
Don’t put sharp skewer sticks on a child’s plate.
Borlotti beans in olive oil
Half a cup boiled borlotti beans
1 small carrot, diced
1 small potato, diced
Soften the onion in olive oil for 3 minutes.
Add the carrot and potato and toss for 3 minutes, then add the tomato.
Add the beans and hot water; cook over a low heat for 25 minutes.
Leave to cool in the pot and serve lukewarm or at room temperature.
Olive oil dishes taste better after resting.
Baked vegetable pasta
Half a cup short pasta (fusilli, penne)
Half a cup small broccoli florets
Preheat the oven to 190 °C. Boil the pasta, add the broccoli for the last 3 minutes and drain together.
Toast the flour in butter for 1 minute, then add the milk gradually, stirring until thick, to make a béchamel.
Mix the pasta and broccoli with the béchamel and put in a small baking dish.
Sprinkle with kashar and bake for 15 minutes until the cheese is golden.
Let cool a little and serve.
Vegetable lentil köfte fingers
3 tablespoons grated carrot
3 tablespoons rolled oats
Roughly mash the lentils with a fork, add the other ingredients and knead.
Shape the mixture into finger-shaped köfte.
Bake on a lined tray for 20 minutes, turning halfway.
Serve with a yogurt sauce.
One of the finger foods that support a child’s self-feeding.
Homemade vegetable soup (chunky)
1 tablespoon vermicelli
Cut the vegetables into 1 cm cubes.
Soften the onion in butter, add the vegetables and toss for 3 minutes.
Add the hot water and cook for 15 minutes.
Add the vermicelli and cook 8 more minutes.
Let cool and serve with the pieces left whole.
At this age, giving soup in small pieces instead of blending supports chewing.
Cheese omelette roll
2 tablespoons lor or white cheese (desalted)
Melt the butter in a wide pan and pour in the egg in a thin layer.
Cook covered over a low heat for 3–4 minutes until the top sets.
Sprinkle with the cheese and parsley, roll up, slice and serve with tomato slices.
Soak white cheese in water for 1 hour to reduce its salt.
Apple and carrot muffins
1 ripe banana, mashed
1 small apple and 1 small carrot, grated
Preheat the oven to 180 °C; put paper cases in the muffin tin.
Whisk the banana, egg and olive oil.
Add the apple and carrot; sift in the flour, baking powder and cinnamon and mix.
Fill the cases two-thirds full and bake for 20–22 minutes until a cocktail stick comes out clean.
Cool on a wire rack.
Ripe banana gives sweetness instead of sugar.
Baked fish patties
100 g boneless sea bass or whiting
1 boiled potato
Preheat the oven to 200 °C. Steam the fish for 8 minutes and check for bones.
Mash the fish and potato; add the dill and egg yolk.
Shape small patties and coat in breadcrumbs.
Bake on a lined tray for 15–18 minutes until golden.
Check for bones twice.
Fruit yogurt ice lollies (sugar-free)
1 cup frozen strawberries or peaches
Blend all the ingredients until smooth.
Divide the mixture among ice-lolly moulds or small pots.
Freeze for at least 4 hours.
Take out 5 minutes before serving.
Also soothing for teething children in hot weather.
1 month in the freezer.
Homemade chicken nuggets (oven-baked)
200 g chicken breast, finger-sized pieces
1 cup crushed unsweetened cornflakes
Mix the chicken with yogurt and leave in the fridge for 30 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 200 °C; mix the cornflakes, kashar and spices.
Coat the chicken pieces well in this mixture and arrange on a lined tray.
Bake for 18–20 minutes, turning halfway, until completely cooked inside.
Serve with a yogurt and dill sauce.
Breading the chicken together with your child increases their interest in the meal.
48 hours in the fridge; can be frozen before cooking.
Vegetable pide
Half a teaspoon instant yeast
3 tablespoons finely chopped red pepper, mushroom and tomato
Knead the flour, yeast, water and olive oil, cover and leave to rise for 40 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 220 °C; divide the dough in 2 and roll into boat shapes.
Divide the vegetables and kashar down the middle and fold in the edges.
Bake for 12–15 minutes until the edges are golden.
Slice and serve.
Let your child decorate their own pide.
